Visitor returns rendered template as a bare string (not a dict) and original mixed-case content is preserved end-to-end (regression guard for issue #350)

```python title="Python"
from html_to_markdown import convert

def main() -> None:
    class _TestVisitor:
        def __init__(self) -> None:
            self.context_errors: list[str] = []
            self.context_reads = 0
        def _record_dict_shaped_context(self, label, ctx) -> bool:  # noqa: ANN001
            # The bridge's fallback arm builds a real PyDict, which answers mapping access
            # (MAP), iterates to its own keys (LIST) and is subscriptable (INDEX). The generated
            # #[pyclass] the stub declares does none of the three. Checking the shape rather than
            # a name is what catches a dict whose keys collide with the declared surface.
            if not isinstance(ctx, dict):
                return False
            keys = sorted(ctx)
            indexed = ctx[keys[0]] if keys else None
            self.context_errors.append(
                f"{label}: context is dict-shaped, not the class the binding declares "
                f"(iterates to {keys!r}, subscript {keys[:1]!r} -> {indexed!r})"
            )
            return True
        def _probe_node_context(self, ctx) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
            self.context_reads += 1
            if self._record_dict_shaped_context("_probe_node_context", ctx):
                return
            for name in (
                "node_type",
                "tag_name",
                "depth",
                "index_in_parent",
                "parent_tag",
                "is_inline",
            ):
                try:
                    getattr(ctx, name)
                except AttributeError as exc:
                    self.context_errors.append(f"{name}: {exc}")
            for name in (
                "attributes",
                "into_owned",
            ):
                try:
                    getattr(ctx, name)()
                except AttributeError as exc:
                    self.context_errors.append(f"{name}: {exc}")
        def visit_link(self, ctx, href, text, title):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202, ARG002
            self._probe_node_context(ctx)
            return f'[{text}](https://new-cdn.com/file.pdf)'
    html = '<a href="https://old-cdn.com/file.pdf">Download</a>'
    _visitor = _TestVisitor()
    result = convert(html, visitor=_visitor)
    assert not _visitor.context_errors, (
        "visitor context is missing attributes the generated binding declares: "
        + "; ".join(_visitor.context_errors)
    )
    assert _visitor.context_reads > 0, "no visitor callback ever received a context object"
    print(result.content)

main()
```
